title: How a tree is grown and read
summary: Leaves, greedy splits, stopping, inference, and pruning.

choices.text: A leaf stores the prediction: a class or class distribution, or a number in regression. A logit is a different object, the log-odds w·x+b inside logistic regression, not a name for a leaf.
Training searches every possible tree and returns a globally optimal partition of the features.
Growth stops for rules you set: a maximum depth, too few samples left to split, or a node that is already pure.
The usual trainer grows the tree greedily, picking at each node a feature and a threshold that most improve a split criterion such as Gini or entropy (classification) or variance (regression).
Pruning, or a hard depth limit, reduces variance. An unpruned tree is free to memorize the training rows.
Inference starts at the root and follows the test in each internal node until a leaf, which supplies the prediction.
